processing: No account of the method is published. It is sold as a premium green tea, which means fixing, shaping and drying without oxidation.
harvest_season: Not documented; premium greens of this class are typically picked in spring.
appearance_dry: Described only as neatly shaped and green.
appearance_liquor: Not documented; typically clear yellow-green for a premium green.
appearance_wet: Not documented; typically tender green leaf.
taste_profile: Described by its promoters as strongly fragrant and mellow, without off-notes; no independent tasting record is available.

brewing.notes: A general method for premium green tea, not one specific to this tea.

vintage_note: Not documented in detail. Normal practice for premium green tea applies: buy the current year's spring harvest and drink it within about a year.
description:
Longzhu Cuiyu is a green tea from Longzhu village in Dunhao town, Kaizhou district, Chongqing. It is listed among Chongqing's specialty teas and is linked to a local company, Kaizhou Longzhu Tea.

The gardens are described as sitting at about 800 metres. The method is not published, so all that can be said is that it is sold as a premium green.

The seller's description promises strong fragrance and a mellow taste. Brew it as any premium green and see whether it delivers.

The name turns up in two forms, Cuiyu ('emerald jade') and Cuiya ('emerald bud'); the first is the one used in accounts of this tea. Do not confuse it with jasmine dragon pearls, which share the 'dragon pearl' name and nothing else.
history: Promotional accounts claim that Longzhu tea was tribute to the court in the Tang and Qing dynasties and that it is now exported to more than ten countries. Neither claim has independent support, and they should be read as local tradition. Little else is documented about when the present tea took shape.
